lessons: No new material fact surfaced since the 2026-08-01 ad-hoc review: Q3 FY2026 results (the next real test) have not been reported. The operative facts remain the Q2 2026 beat-and-raise (guide to $9.25-$9.75, synergy target to $350M) already captured in that review.

This review's one substantive addition is the price anchor: entry_price has been null since 2026-06-01 and no tracking_price was ever established across the 30d or ad-hoc reviews, leaving the record unscoreable for three months. This review establishes tracking_price at the same $123.35 indicative figure the original thesis itself used (MarketBeat, 2026-05-29), so future reviews measure from one fixed point.

Against that anchor, BG has drifted modestly lower (-3.16%) while the S&P 500 rose slightly (+0.41%), a small relative underperformance (-3.58pp) that runs in the direction the original Watchlist caution expected -- even though the underlying earnings news (beat-and-raise, synergies ahead of plan, a completed $2B buyback) ran the other way. Adjudicating this by name: the price hasn't followed the good news yet, which is itself informative and worth watching into Q3, not an argument that the earnings surprise didn't matter.

Was the decision right for the right reason, the wrong reason, or wrong despite good process? Too early to say cleanly. The compound forecast (beat without a raise) was falsified on its discretionary half, which is a genuine miss on that one forecast -- but the Watchlist call itself (not a long, not a short, no proven edge, negative risk/reward at the indicative price) has not been falsified, since price has not rallied to validate the bull case the beat-and-raise might have supported.

Did the catalyst happen? Yes (Q2 results, on schedule). Did the risks materialize? The Viterra-integration risk did not (synergies ahead of plan); the Brazil-tax risk is not assessable this review for lack of fresh primary data -- flagged as a gap to close before the 180d review, not silently carried forward as 'no change'.

Web sources used and dated: FinancialContent/StockStory (BG price, 2026-09-01); S&P 500 level via aggregated search results dated to 2026-06-01 and 2026-09-01 close; general Bunge Q2 2026 coverage via BigGo Finance/TradingView/Seeking Alpha (2026-07-29, unchanged from the prior review). All web-sourced, indicative/unverified.

Single most important takeaway: the pre-mortem's blind spot identified at the ad-hoc review still holds three-plus weeks later -- none of its six kill-criteria attacks anticipated the company simply outperforming, and Q3 (the next real test of whether that outperformance is durable) is still pending.

learning.rule_for_future: A compound forecast joining a near-certain event (a beat, given five consecutive prior beats) to a discretionary management decision (whether to raise guidance) should be split into two separate forecasts -- the discretionary half is what actually carries the thesis, and its failure gets diluted when the easy half succeeds alongside it.

pre_mortem_check.notes: Unchanged from the 2026-08-01 ad-hoc finding, now reaffirmed by three more weeks without a reversal: FALSE COMFORT. The pre-mortem returned 'Survives' with a zero haircut, but the thesis has been at-risk since the Q2 print. None of its six kill_criteria_attack items (Brazil tax, FCF staying negative, spread retrace, goodwill impairment, covenant breach, governance disqualifier) anticipated the actual surprise -- the company simply outperforming (beat, raise, synergies ahead of plan, completed buyback). A red-team that attacks only the ways a cautious call could be too optimistic did not catch the way this one was, if anything, too pessimistic about near-term execution.
